cards.meaning: Loop once per item in a known list
cards.example: for arg in one two three; do echo "$arg"; done
cards.notes: You already have the list. One pass per item.

cards.meaning: Build the list from a command’s output
cards.example: for file in "$(find . -type l)"; do echo "$file"; done | sort
cards.notes: Quoting matters; piping the whole loop’s output is allowed.

cards.example: for i in {1..5}; do echo $i; done

cards.meaning: Loop while the test at the top is true (status 0)
cards.notes: Count unknown beforehand. Give counters a starting value.

cards.meaning: Opposite of while — body while false; stop when true

cards.notes: With for i in {1..5} and break at 3, prints 1 2 3.

cards.meaning: Skip the rest of this pass; go to the next item
cards.notes: Does not exit the loop — only this iteration.

cards.meaning: Known list vs unknown count / condition-driven
cards.example: for x in list · while [ cond ]
cards.notes: for = you have the items. while/until = keep going based on a test.
